new_entities.name: Catch-up HPV vaccination
new_entities.description: HPV vaccination delivered in catch-up cohorts after the earliest routine adolescent target ages.

new_entities.name: Cervical precancerous lesions
new_entities.description: High-grade cervical intraepithelial lesions and related precancerous cervical abnormalities.

edges.effect_quant: Catch-up HPV vaccination still lowers high-grade cervical lesion risk, but the benefit is smaller than vaccination before sexual debut because more participants have already encountered vaccine-type HPV.
edges.population: adolescents and young women vaccinated in catch-up HPV programs or late-adolescent trial cohorts
edges.mechanism: Even in catch-up settings, HPV vaccination can prevent persistent infection and progression to CIN2+ or CIN3+ for women not yet infected with the relevant oncogenic types. The effect attenuates with increasing prior exposure, which is why catch-up helps but does not match pre-exposure adolescent vaccination.
edges.summary: The strongest catch-up signal is that protection remains real but partial. Australian lesion-typing data show a falling share of HPV16/18-driven CIN3/AIS in vaccine-eligible young women, while the large PATRICIA trial confirms meaningful efficacy against cervical precancer in the total vaccinated cohort that approximates catch-up populations.
edges.caveats: Catch-up vaccination is intrinsically more heterogeneous than routine preadolescent vaccination because prior HPV exposure varies widely. This edge is about lesion reduction, not the larger long-term cancer-prevention effect seen when vaccination happens before sexual debut.

evidence.notes: HPV16/18 prevalence in high-grade cervical lesions in an Australian population offered catch-up HPV vaccination.

evidence.citation: ApterD et al 2015 Clin Vaccine Immunol
evidence.notes: Efficacy of human papillomavirus 16 and 18 (HPV-16/18) AS04-adjuvanted vaccine against cervical infection and precancer in young women: final event-driven analysis of the randomized, double-blind PATRICIA trial.

effect_quant.comparator: CIN2+ irrespective of HPV DNA in the total vaccinated cohort versus control

evidence.notes: Overall efficacy of HPV-16/18 AS04-adjuvanted vaccine against grade 3 or greater cervical intraepithelial neoplasia: 4-year end-of-study analysis of the randomised, double-blind PATRICIA trial.

effect_quant.comparator: all CIN3+ in the total vaccinated cohort versus control
